learning_objective: 🎯 Welcome to Python Data Science! Learn how to create, manipulate, and analyze structured data using powerful Pandas Series and DataFrames.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Pandas is an open-source Python library used for high-performance data manipulation and analysis. The name comes from 'Panel Data'. You must import it using: `import pandas as pd`.

A Series is a one-dimensional array capable of holding any data type. Think of it like a single column in an Excel sheet. It has two main components: the actual data values, and their associated labels (Index).
A DataFrame is a two-dimensional, size-mutable, tabular data structure with labeled axes (rows and columns). It's exactly like an SQL table or an Excel spreadsheet!
You can create DataFrames from various sources: a Python dictionary of lists, a list of dictionaries, a 2D NumPy array, or even another existing Series.

To extract data, we use slicing. `.loc[]` is used when you want to access rows/columns by their actual string LABELS. `.iloc[]` is used when you want to access them by their integer POSITION (index 0, 1, 2...).

fun_activity.title: 📊 The Digital Report Card
fun_activity.instructions: Open Python and create a dictionary: `data = {'Name':['Amit', 'Neha'], 'Marks':[95, 98]}`. Now type `df = pd.DataFrame(data)` and print it. You just created a digital, perfectly formatted report card table in two lines of code!

exam_tips: 📌 DataFrames are value-mutable AND size-mutable (you can change data and add columns). Series are value-mutable but size-IMMUTABLE (you cannot add new elements once created).
📌 When using slicing like `df.loc['A':'C']`, the endpoint 'C' is INCLUDED. But in integer slicing `df.iloc[0:3]`, the endpoint 3 is EXCLUDED (it only prints 0, 1, 2).
📌 Memorize common DataFrame attributes: `df.shape` gives (rows, columns), `df.size` gives total elements, and `df.columns` gives column names.
quick_recap: ⭐ A Series is basically a single column, while a DataFrame is a collection of Series side-by-side.
⭐ The default index in Pandas always starts at 0, unless you explicitly provide custom labels.
⭐ `import pandas as pd` is the universal standard alias used by data scientists worldwide.
